title: Create a Capped Virtual Card
objectives: Name your virtual card clearly, such as Google Cloud or Hotel Trip, to identify its purpose
Set a spending cap to limit the total amount that can be charged to the card
Set an end date so the card expires automatically when it is no longer needed

analogy.title: The Labeled Gift Envelope
analogy.text: Think of creating a virtual card like preparing a labeled gift envelope with cash inside. You write 'Google Cloud' or 'Hotel Trip' on the front so you instantly know its purpose, just as you would label an envelope for a specific person or occasion. You put only a set amount inside—that's your spending cap—which prevents overspending and surprise charges. Finally, you write an expiry date on the envelope—after this date it can no longer be used. The name organizes, the limit protects your budget, and the end date automatically closes the envelope when you're done.

pitch30Seconds: To create a capped virtual card, give it a clear name like Google Cloud or Hotel Trip so you can track its spend. Next, set a spending cap that limits the total amount that can be charged—this prevents overruns. Then choose an end date when the card automatically expires, so you avoid recurring surprise charges after a trial or trip ends. Name, cap, and end date together give you safe, organized spending.
keyPoints: Name your card for its purpose, like Google Cloud or Hotel Trip, to organize and track spend
Spending cap limits the total amount chargeable and prevents overspending
End date automatically expires the card to avoid surprise future charges
Test mode creates sample cards only — no real cards are issued and no real money moves

recallQuiz.question: Why should you name your virtual card like 'Google Cloud' or 'Hotel Trip'?
options: To identify its purpose and easily track spend
To increase the spending cap automatically
To share the card with other users
To extend the card's expiry date
recallQuiz.explanation: A clear name helps you organize and track spend by purpose.

recallQuiz.question: What does setting a spending cap do?
options: It extends the card's validity forever
It limits the total amount that can be charged to prevent overruns
It automatically categorizes transactions for accounting
recallQuiz.explanation: The cap sets a maximum total chargeable amount to avoid surprise charges.

recallQuiz.question: Why is setting an end date important?
options: It increases the cap before the trial ends
It automatically expires the card to avoid recurring charges after a trip or trial
It lets you rename the card later
It is required to activate test mode
recallQuiz.explanation: An end date ensures the card expires automatically so you avoid future surprise charges.

testModeNote: This simulation runs in test mode with sample cards only. No real cards are issued and no real money moves.
